proposal.problem:
Malaysian micro and small cafes repeatedly check ingredient stock, request quotations and decide when to reorder. The owner often has to reconcile separate records before approving a purchase. Arithmetic mistakes, late ordering and undocumented decisions can disrupt service and add administrative work.

DecisionOS focuses on milk replenishment in a fictional cafe. The reference case has 18 litres in stock, estimated use of 12 litres per day and a three-day minimum coverage threshold. Current coverage is therefore 1.5 days. One supplier offers a lower price but estimates delivery after available stock runs out; another offers earlier delivery at a higher price. Price alone is insufficient for the decision.

The affected users are cafe owners and purchasing managers. The prototype brings stock evidence, delivery assumptions and quotation arithmetic into one transparent approval journey. It aims to reduce repetitive comparison work while preserving owner control and a traceable record.

This is a problem hypothesis supported by the challenge brief and a synthetic scenario, not a completed SME field study. A timed usability comparison is planned. No real customer, employee or company records are used, and no business savings or stockout reductions have been measured.
proposal.solution:
Orbyte DecisionOS combines a working operational workflow with an optional AI scenario layer. A user initiates an inventory check; our mock Orbyte-style connector retrieves synthetic inventory and quotations. Python rules calculate coverage, cost and delivery risk. An owner selects or rejects an option, records a reason and receives a persistent purchase-order draft and audit trail after approval. No supplier is contacted and no payment is made.

The UI exposes the RM90 premium for earlier estimated milk delivery. Backend role checks, snapshot validation and idempotency protect approval and draft creation.

The optional MiroFish adapter explores a delivery delay or menu-price change through fictional stakeholder perspectives. Its source is pinned and HTTP contracts are tested. A separate environment is installed, and small Gemini API verification calls succeeded. A genuine run still needs a valid Zep key and a checked provider quota. The UI shows unavailable status rather than invented results. Agent narratives will not replace arithmetic or become unsupported forecasts.

The approach applies database, API and cloud-deployment concepts relevant to the workshops. All mandatory team workshops are complete. The project now runs in Replit; the approval workflow and reload persistence were verified there. The priority is a complete operational journey.
proposal.stack:
Frontend: Next.js 16.4.2, React 19.3.1, TypeScript 5.9.3 and Tailwind CSS 4.3.3. Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.135.1, Pydantic 2.12.5 and SQLAlchemy 2.0.48. SQLite stores business records, decision snapshots, approvals, order drafts, audit events and simulation requests. Money uses integer sen; quantities and rules use Decimal.

Next.js proxies API requests to FastAPI. The mock connector is our own documented interface assumption, not an official Orbyte API. Optional simulation requests are processed by a separate local worker against MiroFish commit 7657031ac01184afe2cb220f5ee3545573b5e843. DecisionOS external execution remains disabled; the separate Gemini provider completed small verification calls, while Zep authentication remains incomplete.

In Replit, 33 backend tests, three component tests, TypeScript checks, the production build and four Playwright tests passed using installed Chromium 152. Native-browser checks verified approval and persistence. See Appendix A for architecture.

Replit: source imported and development preview verified on 23 October 2026. See the proof-of-use record. Sponsor-credit status is unconfirmed. No GPU workload has been executed; RunPod is not applicable.
proposal.design:
The design starts with one recurring owner task: deciding which supplier can replenish a critical ingredient in time. A synthetic journey makes the data, trigger and decision explicit before adding broader modules. The interface places quote costs, estimated delivery and missing information beside owner approval controls; roles are clearly labelled as simulated.

The working local prototype has been iterated through automated backend/component checks and direct browser use. Approval, rejection, reload persistence and mobile navigation were checked. A timed study with consenting testers is still planned; no interviews or user validation are claimed.

Phase 2 work will validate the problem with SMEs, measure task completion against a manual baseline, and refine the workflow from observed errors. Real deployment would require authentication, tenant isolation, migrations, backups and a reviewed privacy process. The synthetic Replit development preview now runs and passed its approval and reload checks.

The main integration risk is unreliable or costly simulation execution. Deterministic procurement remains usable when MiroFish is offline. A small synthetic run will be measured before any AI result is demonstrated; the operational workflow remains usable without it.
proposal.sdg:
Primary: SDG 8, targets 8.2 and 8.3.

8.2 concerns productivity through technological upgrading and innovation. DecisionOS aims to reduce repetitive procurement administration.

8.3 includes productive activities, entrepreneurship and SME growth. Traceable owner-controlled workflows are a proposed contribution, not evidence of policy-level impact.

Source: UN DESA, Goal 8, https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal8 (reviewed 22 Oct 2026).
proposal.baseline:
Estimated planning baseline: 10 minutes to complete a correct manual comparison, approval record and procurement draft for one shortage case.

This is a team planning assumption, not an observed measurement or published benchmark. Replace it with the median of actual manual trials before making a measured improvement claim.

Reference operational input: 18 / 12 = 1.5 days of stock coverage. This is calculated from synthetic data.
proposal.kpi:
Primary KPI: percentage reduction in median time to complete a correct procurement draft, calculated as (manual median - DecisionOS median) / manual median x 100.

Guardrails: arithmetic errors per task; percentage of approved drafts with actor, reason and timestamp; unassisted completion rate. Use identical synthetic tasks, alternate task order and report sample size and help given.
proposal.target:
Proposed Phase 2 target: at least 30% lower median task time; at a 10-minute baseline, this means no more than 7 minutes.

Guardrails: zero reference-case arithmetic errors, 100% complete approval records and at least 80% unassisted pilot completion.

These are proposed targets. No productivity gain, waste reduction, revenue change or stockout probability has been measured.

declaration.architecture:
The Next.js interface sends same-origin API requests to FastAPI. A documented mock Orbyte-style connector retrieves synthetic business inventory and quotations from SQLite through SQLAlchemy. Deterministic Python rules calculate stock coverage, quote totals and delivery-risk comparisons. An owner approves or rejects a stored decision snapshot. Approval, a synthetic purchase-order draft and audit records commit atomically; idempotency prevents duplicate drafts for the same decision.

MiroFish is optional and isolated behind an original HTTP adapter. Persistent simulation requests are claimed by a separate local worker, which records source identifiers, status, errors and genuine completed reports only. Its upstream environment is installed locally at a pinned commit. Small Gemini API verification calls succeeded, but the locally saved Zep value is masked and invalid. No genuine simulation has completed; DecisionOS external execution remains disabled.

The running prototype uses local SQLite and explicitly simulated roles. The authenticated Replit workspace runs the synthetic development preview and passed the approval workflow. No production deployment is claimed. Appendix A shows the component boundary.
declaration.review: Codex assisted extensively with implementation, tests, debugging and documentation. Executed checks include 33 backend tests, three component tests, TypeScript checks and a production build. Replit Agent briefly inspected the import before being stopped. Native-browser checks covered approval, rejection, persistence and mobile navigation. Four Playwright tests passed in Replit with installed Chromium. Registered-team review, adaptation and understanding have not yet been confirmed. Before signing, members must inspect the code, reproduce the journey, review assumptions and licence obligations, and record their changes. AI-generated output must not be treated as reviewed merely because automated tests passed.
declaration.replaceability: Replit was used to import, install, build, run and test the synthetic prototype on 23 October 2026. Proof includes workspace screenshots and passing tests. Sponsor-credit use is unconfirmed. The application can also run locally on Python and Node.js, so hosting is replaceable. RunPod was not used because no GPU workload was executed. Our mock connector does not use Orbyte production APIs.
declaration.privacy:
The application is intended only for invented business, supplier and user records. It stores synthetic inventory, quotations, decision reasons, approvals, draft orders and audit events in local SQLite. Free-text fields can accept typed text, so testers must not enter personal or confidential information. The current operational app sends no business data to an external AI provider. Separate tiny Gemini API checks used only test prompts. Enabling MiroFish would send the declared synthetic scenario through the separate service to approved LLM/Zep providers.

Secrets are excluded from Git and never exposed in the frontend. Local data remains until the operator deliberately resets it; no automatic retention schedule exists. Demo roles are not authentication. Public or real-data use requires real identity, access controls, retention and privacy review. Team contact details in the submission are separate from application data.
declaration.risks:
MiroFish has not completed a genuine run, so live compatibility, latency and cost are unverified. Social-agent narratives can be biased, incomplete or mistaken and are not calibrated forecasts. Missing report sections stay empty; failed runs produce an explicit error. Deterministic arithmetic is independent of AI. Requests have time limits and cancellation is best effort; upstream graph/report work can continue. DecisionOS external execution remains disabled; Free-tier eligibility and limits need confirmation before live use.

The operational prototype uses selectable demo roles and local SQLite, with no production authentication, migrations or external purchasing. Delivery and consumption are estimates. Four Playwright tests passed in Replit using installed Chromium; local macOS startup remains restricted. SME validation, production hosting and genuine MiroFish execution remain pending.
